pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Dark regions on the neck exhibit large polygonal geometries with defined but slightly softened pixel gradients at edges. The posterior and lower flank shows a transition to significantly smaller, high-frequency dark islands with irregular, fragmented boundaries.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Light-colored pathways form a continuous network of varying thickness. On the neck, corridors are wide with distinct multi-way junction nodes. On the lower flank, the network thins to fine lines separating dense clusters of small dark patches.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: The dorsal mane presents as a continuous dark brown line with frequent, low-height vertical peaks forming a serrated 1D profile against the background.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: A large, localized region of pigment attenuation is visible on the upper mid-flank. This area shows a loss of contrast between patches and corridors, presenting as a grayish-white textural disruption.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Three avian organisms (oxpeckers) are perched on the subject: two on the upper shoulder/dorsal ridge and one on the upper tail region. A large area of de-pigmented skin/textural disruption is present on the upper-mid flank.
other_distinctive_markers: Highly distinct spatial heterogeneity in patch size across the torso, ranging from large macro-patches on the neck to micro-patches on the lower hindquarter.
